tier_1_method_card.score_function: Leave-one-out residuals determine the interval width, while leave-one-out predictions at the test point are also used to account for fitted-function variability.
tier_1_method_card.coverage_guarantee: With exchangeable training samples and a training algorithm that treats observations symmetrically, Jackknife+ has rigorous distribution-free predictive-coverage guarantees; the abstract also reports a K-fold cross-validation extension.
tier_1_method_card.exchangeability_assumption: Exchangeable training samples; the method's guarantee is stated for algorithms treating training points symmetrically.
tier_1_method_card.computational_cost: Leave-one-out fitting/prediction for all observations; the allowed Jackknife+ search record describes this as requiring leave-one-out refits and notes the resulting cost relative to split conformal.

input_features.value: Ten in-game variables for the running home-team win probability model.
Historical data from the last seven NFL seasons obtained through the league API.

tier_2_model_card.output_distribution: Running binary win probability for the home team in an NFL game.
tier_2_model_card.calibration_method: The paper reports that the iWinRNFL probabilities are well-calibrated; its abstract does not name a separate post-hoc calibration procedure.
tier_2_model_card.known_biases: Do not assume sportsbook probabilities are automatically efficient: the allowed football-market papers report exploitable odds/line effects, including a claimed football-market inefficiency and a home-underdog strategy exceeding the stated break-even threshold in the studied sample.
tier_2_model_card.data_requirements: NFL league-API play-by-play over multiple historical seasons; the model is described as using seven seasons of detailed play-by-play data.

tier_3_data_source_card.coverage: Seven historical NFL seasons in the iWinRNFL study; the related NFLSimulatoR paper describes sampling from previous NFL football seasons.
tier_3_data_source_card.granularity: Detailed play-by-play data, suitable for in-game state updates; NFLSimulatoR likewise operates on plays and drives.
tier_3_data_source_card.update_frequency: Not specified in the allowed abstracts; the source description identifies a league API and historical play-by-play rather than a refresh schedule.
tier_3_data_source_card.known_gaps: The NFL data description does not establish NCAAF, FCS, transfer-portal, NIL, or conference-realignment coverage. The allowed college-football search returns 32 records, including Elo and point-spread work, but this does not establish a conformal NCAAF deployment.

ncaaf_specifics.distribution_shift_type: Temporal and covariate shift are the relevant unaddressed risks: Jackknife+ requires exchangeability for its stated guarantee, while the college-football records include season-/era-dependent Elo and point-spread modeling rather than a demonstrated transfer-portal, FCS/FBS, NIL, or realignment adjustment.

calibration_analysis.isotonic_regression_limits: Do not treat a generic monotone recalibration as sufficient evidence of validity: the allowed Kalshi study finds calibration changes sharply with time-to-expiry and product type, so calibration must be conditioned on those variables rather than price alone.

sgp_parlay_data.correlation_model: Use the contemporaneous product of leg prices as the reference, but do not assume independence is correct: the allowed Kalshi study finds cross-game parlays systematically overpriced relative to that product, with overpricing increasing with leg count.
